limitations: P1 — A.16 selects the wrong coefficient of y — Counterevidence: The correct determinant formula (3.5b) and abstract definition remain valid in the example. This is not an Algorithm1 full-trajectory counterexample or a refutation of Theorem1.1.
P2 — Filter zero projected directions before normalization — Counterevidence: Lemma4.1 already defines the correct nonzero candidate set W; its mathematical argument does not normalize zero vectors.

P3 — LemmaA.2 places the factorial on the wrong side — Counterevidence: The subsequent proof of Proposition3.5 uses sum=(1/k!) derivative, which is the correct normalization; positive global factors do not change roots.
P4 — The projected-zero target leaves alpha undefined — Counterevidence: BB^dagger A=0 makes every selected-column residual equal A; the desired bound is trivial there.

P5 — The Laguerre root lemma needs a nonconstant degree range — Counterevidence: Theorem1.4 uses deletion order d-k with positive retained k, hence at most d-1; this example does not refute its bound.

repair.content:
Replace every mu_(j,c1,rhat) remaining after the y derivative in A.16 by mu_(j,c1,khat).

Restrict candidate preparation and polynomial evaluation to Qb_i!=0 and Pc_i!=0 before normalizing. The rank assumptions ensure enough admissible directions until the target size is reached.

Use sum_(|S|=d-k) det(xI-M_SS)=(1/k!) partial_x^k det(xI-M), equivalently move k! to multiply the sum.

Handle BB^dagger A=0 separately; define alpha only when its denominator is positive.

State beta*d/(1+beta)<k<d, or separately define and handle degree-exhaustion cases. Treat beta=0 minimization at b=1 by a one-sided limit.
